title: Stuff You Should Know July 4th Extravaganza, Part 2: Baseball and Apple Pie
summary: Part two of a live July 4th special recorded before a studio audience at SiriusXM studios in New York City. Josh and Chuck explain the chemistry of black powder, fireworks, sparklers and aerial shells, including salts used for colors. Guest Hallie Haglin tells a true story of a Denver neighborhood fire started by a thrown smoke bomb, and recounts fireworks factory explosions and fireworks fires abroad. The hosts then trace the history of the American Dream from John Winthrop's City upon a Hill sermon through the Declaration of Independence, Tocqueville, Thoreau, the Depression, the New Deal, the 1950s, the 1960s civil rights era, the 1970s, Reagan, and John Quelch's critique of consumerism. Guest Joe Randazzo of The Onion reads satirical headlines from the 1783 Onion issue and Ben Franklin's invented-items column. The episode closes with thanks to fans, crew and partners.

entities.name: Collection of the Most Important Military Techniques

segments.title: Opening banter and setup
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open part two of the live July 4th show, joke about the recording and the audience, and set up the fireworks topic.

segments.title: How fireworks work: black powder chemistry
segments.summary: The hosts explain black powder (potassium nitrate, charcoal, sulfur), its Chinese origins with the 1044 military text, and how the oxidizer and fuel produce light, heat and explosive force.

segments.title: Sparklers, aerial shells and firework colors
segments.summary: They describe sparkler composition with sugar and metal dust, how aerial shells with stars, lifting charges and breaking charges work, and which metal salts make which colors (copper blue, strontium red, sodium yellow, calcium orange, barium green).

segments.title: Hallie Haglin on fireworks disasters
segments.summary: Guest Hallie Haglin lists fireworks factory explosions and fires in the Netherlands, the Philippines, Denmark, and Beijing's Mandarin Hotel, and cites US firework-related death statistics from the Consumer Product Safety Commission.

segments.title: Denver smoke bomb tree fire story
segments.summary: Hallie tells a personal story from childhood in Denver in which her brother threw a smoke bomb that landed in a juniper tree, starting a fire that spread to neighboring trees and roofs.

segments.title: Homemade bottle rocket guns
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh talk about childhood experiments with bottle rockets, including Chuck's homemade bottle rocket guns built from modified rubber band guns.

segments.title: History of the American Dream
segments.summary: The hosts trace the American Dream from John Winthrop's 1630 City upon a Hill sermon through the Declaration of Independence, Tocqueville's observations, Thoreau's Walden, immigration and westward expansion, and the shift toward wealth as success.

segments.title: American Dream from Depression to consumerism
segments.summary: The American Dream is followed through the Depression, FDR's New Deal, postwar suburbs, Martin Luther King Jr.'s redefinition, the 1970s slump, Reagan's version, and John Quelch's critique of acquisition, ending with a quote from James Truslow Adams.

segments.title: Thanks and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts thank the live audience, guests, crew, and partners, plug the video recording, and sign off with a fireworks safety reminder.
